scenes.narration: Two runners on a track, one twice as fast. If there is a loop, they must collide. But why must?

scenes.headline: One step, [two steps]
scenes.caption: round one
scenes.narration: |While fast exists and fast dot next exists, keep running. That double check is the guard: if either is missing we've reached the end of the track, so there was no loop. |Slow moves to >node ^two. |Fast moves twice, to >node ^three. %The gap between them is one node now, where a moment ago it was zero.

lines.detail: Stop if the hare runs out of track.

scenes.premise: A running track made of linked nodes. Both runners start together: the tortoise moves one node per round, the hare moves two.

scenes.headline: Round two, [into the bend]
scenes.caption: the hare comes round
scenes.narration: |Slow moves to >node ^three. Fast moves two again: node three to node four, and then four points back to two, |so >the hare lands on ^node two. It has been round the bend, and it's now sitting behind the tortoise. %The gap is two. On a track with no loop the hare would have fallen off by now, and instead it's lapping.

lines.detail: Hare: two more, and round the loop.

scenes.premise: A running track made of linked nodes. Both runners start together: the tortoise moves one node per round, the hare moves two.

scenes.headline: And they [meet]
scenes.caption: both on node four
scenes.narration: |Slow steps to >node four. |Fast goes two: node two to node three, then three to four, so >it lands on ^node four as well. |Slow equals fast, so |we return True. There's a cycle. %One pass, %no extra memory, and no list of visited nodes anywhere.

lines.detail: Tortoise: one step, to node four.
Hare: two steps, also to node four.
